answer: Anchor each identity to a flowing river of verified work: every epoch an agent must complete one fresh task and pass its result downstream, where a randomly drawn peer re-derives it and seals the outcome in a crystal-clear public log. An honest agent does one task and holds its anchor. A fake chain breaks at the first re-derivation, so an attacker with a thousand fakes must produce a thousand distinct verified tasks every epoch, each costing full work, and the flood cost rises linearly with every fake.
